segments.content:
Chapter 118: 0115 Company Move, Recruiting Employees (Bonus chapter for the Alliance Leader, One-Handed Drifting Smoker)

December 4th, Saturday.

ByteDance and Game Science officially moved into their new offices in the Science Park Building.

Not only did Bian Guanyue come to help, but some classmates from the Yuanpei Program, and even his old high school classmate Wu Meng, also came to join in the fun after hearing the news.

Once you're here, you have to work!

"Where should I put this cactus?"

"Put it over there."

"Damn it, if I'd known I'd have to help mop, I wouldn't have come for anything!"

"We're having barbecue tonight."

"This window is too high, I can't reach it."

"Then don't worry about it."

Bian Guanyue was particularly energetic, working as if she were the one moving into a new home.

Many hands make light work, and the two offices were set up in no time.

Jiang Junlai exclaimed with emotion, "Sigh, you're still the incredible one. I'm still studying freshman core courses, and you've already built such a big company."

Chen Guiliang said, "The price is how many classes I'm going to fail this semester."

"Hahaha!"

Jiang Junlai's psyche was instantly balanced.

"I'll sign up for two fewer classes next semester and come work part-time for you to earn some pocket money," said Yun Fan from the dorm room across the hall.

Chen Guiliang said, "You're welcome anytime."

Deng Chen from the same dorm said, "Seeing your two companies here makes me want to choose computer science as my major. I'll come work for you right after I graduate."

Chen Guiliang put his arm around his shoulder. "Absolutely high salary!"

Zhao Beibei wandered around the office.

Zeng Changgao was filled with envy. He decided that when he became a senior, he would also start his own company.

Wu Meng pulled Bian Guanyue into a corner to talk. "Congratulations, Lady Boss."

"Don't talk nonsense!" Bian Guanyue was all smiles.

There were also seven or eight other Yuanpei classmates who would occasionally come over to talk to Chen Guiliang, or walk around looking and asking questions.

After chatting with Wu Meng, Bian Guanyue walked over to Chen Guiliang and said, "Come outside for a minute."

Chen Guiliang accompanied her to the emergency exit stairwell.

Bian Guanyue asked, "With two companies this big, do you have enough money?"

"It's alright. I got a low-interest loan of 500,000 yuan," Chen Guiliang said. "And *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* has started its online serialization. Although a lot of people are criticizing it, it's already gaining popularity. I'll be able to get a sum of royalties when it gets published soon."

Bian Guanyue took out a UnionPay card. "Take this and use it for now. Just consider it a loan."

Chen Guiliang didn't want to take her money but also found it hard to refuse directly. He joked, "I still owe you a thousand yuan for the clothes. How much are you lending me this time?"

"There's over 600,000 in the card," Bian Guanyue said.

"How much?" Chen Guiliang finally understood what a "little rich girl" was.

Bian Guanyue said, "This is what my grandparents left me. It includes their retirement savings over the years, plus the allowance my dad usually gave them. When my grandpa passed away, he said the title to the old house would go to my aunt, and this money was the dowry he and my grandma saved for me."

Chen Guiliang pushed the bank card back, his expression serious. "That's all the more reason I can't accept it."

"Just take it. It's just sitting in the bank earning interest anyway." Fearing Chen Guiliang would refuse, Bian Guanyue's tone was already a little anxious.

Chen Guiliang decided to lighten the mood, smiling as he said, "What if I lose your whole dowry?"

Bian Guanyue said, "If you lose it all, we'll just slowly earn it back in the future."

Chen Guiliang didn't know what to say.

The money felt too hot to handle, but he was afraid of hurting Bian Guanyue's feelings if he didn't take it.

His phone began to ring.

It was a life-saving call from Li Xunhuan.

"Hello, President Lu." Chen Guiliang gestured for Bian Guanyue to wait a moment.

Li Xunhuan's voice was cheerful. "You're famous again. Lots of newspapers are reporting on you."

"It's alright, I guess," Chen Guiliang said.

The public discussion about Chen Guiliang had died down after he enrolled at Peking University.

But once the *China Youth Daily* published the news about the campus belle competition, Chen Guiliang once again drew attention.

The media reporters discovered that the high school student from six months ago was actually making waves at Peking University again. He had started a business in his freshman year, opening two companies at once, and his website's event was even being reported on by the *China Youth Daily*.

Some newspapers even dug up his "small goal of a hundred million" and discussed with great seriousness how much money Chen Guiliang could earn while still in university.

The most ridiculous were the gossip tabloids, which claimed Chen Guiliang launched the campus belle competition to pursue the Olympic champion Liu Xuan, and was even secretly boosting her votes... their imagination was truly one-of-a-kind. No wonder their papers sold well.

Li Xunhuan said, "I plan to reveal your royalty rate too. It's the highest royalty share in all of China, which is sure to stir up a lot of discussion. We can ride the wave of public opinion and guide the media to focus on your *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*."

"Sounds good." Chen Guiliang desperately needed to sell books to make money.

Li Xunhuan said, "Speed up your writing, increase the frequency of your online posts, and let's aim for a book signing event after your final exams end."

"Isn't that a bit too fast?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Xunhuan said, "Under normal circumstances, we'd need to let it build up more online. But your situation isn't normal. This is a great promotional opportunity."

Chen Guiliang said, "Then let's add more fuel to the fire. When you reveal the royalty rate to the media, also say that my Xiaonei Network has attracted the interest of VCs, and I turned down a valuation of 5 million US dollars."

"Did a VC really value it at 5 million US dollars?" Li Xunhuan asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "It can have."

Li Xunhuan chuckled. "Understood. Once the newspapers publish the story, I'll spread it online. A lot of netizens will definitely be drawn to read your book!"

Whether it happened or not, for the media reporters, it could have happened.

After a few more words, he hung up the phone.

Bian Guanyue, who had been standing by and listening, silently put her bank card back in her pocket. She felt that Chen Guiliang wasn't short on money anymore.

If she were to lend him money now, it would feel like emotional blackmail, and Bian Guanyue didn't like doing that.

"Why are you putting it away? Quick, give it to me," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue mumbled, "But you don't need the money."

Chen Guiliang said, "I really do. Royalties aren't paid out daily, there's a cycle, and there's no guarantee the book will even sell well."

"Then I'm lending it to you. The thousand yuan for the clothes has to be included too!" Bian Guanyue's face instantly lit up with joy.

Sigh, this silly, lovesick woman.

Bian Guanyue didn't mention writing an IOU, and Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to bring it up.

Giving her shares was even more unnecessary; it could easily lead to conflict.

Take Shanda's Boss Chen, for example. He was the largest shareholder, his younger brother was the second largest, and his wife was the third. After the company grew, it needed standardized management. He had to use gentle methods with his brother, while his wife was kicked out of the decision-making circle entirely.

Things like that really hurt relationships. Boss Chen had already handled it extremely well, being able to properly arrange things for his wife and brother.

Like a little follower, Bian Guanyue happily followed Chen Guiliang back to the office, as if she were the one who had just borrowed hundreds of thousands from him.

As they passed the elevator, a young man stepped out.

"Hello, excuse me, where is the ByteDance company?" the young man asked.

Seeing the *Job Market News* in his hand, Chen Guiliang said, "Come with me."

It was already early December. The two part-time programmers from Peking University were about to quit to study for their finals and avoid failing their courses. He had to hire two more junior programmers who at least knew website maintenance and could also do development work with Guo Feng.

Dong Qianqiu had gotten an internship at Microsoft Research Asia and had already been interning there for three days. He also needed to hire another senior programmer.

With the explosive growth of Xiaonei Network's user base, he could no longer rely on just part-time customer service staff; he had to hire a full-time one.

The online version of *Sanguosha* was about to be launched, and that required hiring people too.

Advertising in *Job Market News* was relatively cheap. A front-page recruitment ad cost two to three thousand yuan, while a small blurb tucked away in a corner was only two or three hundred.

Chen Guiliang had posted a 500-yuan ad.

If he couldn't find anyone through the paper, he would have to go to the Beijing Talent Building to rent a booth.

Posting on the Peking University BBS was also an option, but Chen Guiliang felt that Peking University students were too expensive. For entry-level positions, it was more suitable to hire from outside the university.

Walking into the office, Chen Guiliang said, "Give me your resume."

"Excuse me, are you..." The young man hesitated, because Chen Guiliang looked even younger than him.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm the boss of the company."

"Huh?"
